- We need a concrete validation window with pass/fail criteria for throughput and tail latency (we serve customers across peak sale periods).
- A defined "switchback" timeframe if the dedicated fleet causes increased 99th percentile latency or token loss.
- Confirmation of which GPU family will host our model and whether mirror traffic can be routed during the handoff.

I attached a 24-hour traffic sample (DealerBridge_Traffic_Sample.csv) and highlighted our expected concurrency spike (Black Friday-style, though scaled). Can you propose a timeline with gate checks and a rollback plan?

Ellen / Tom—thanks for the sample and for flagging those requirements. Draft plan below; I want to confirm a couple of inputs from you (annotated in the action items).

High-level three-phase migration plan (proposed):

1) Shadow & sizing validation (7 days)
   - Mirror 100% of a subset of production traffic (read-only inference) to dedicated pool.
   - Run synthetic load that reproduces peak concurrency from your CSV for three 1-hour windows across different TTFB profiles.
   - Acceptance criteria: 99th percentile latency <= 1.2x hosted baseline AND < 10% cost token delta (to confirm unit economics).

2) Canary switch (48 hours)
   - Route 5% traffic to dedicated pool, then step to 20% after a successful 3-hour smoke test.
   - Blackout rollback window: next business-day 00:00–04:00 PST reserved as automatic switchback window in case tail latency regresses beyond thresholds.

3) Full switchover & verification (24 hours)
   - Gradual ramp to 100% across 3 increments, with continuous KV/prefix cache warm-ups and hourly acceptance checks.

Acceptance & rollback gates (short):
   - Throughput: dedicated pool must sustain >= 1.8x expected average token/s during peak samples for 1 hour.
   - Tail latency: P99 must not exceed 450ms (absolute) or 1.2x your hosted baseline (whichever is lower).
   - Error budget: <0.5% spike in 5xx rates sustained for >10 minutes.

Requested inputs / actions for DealerBridge:
   - Confirm which 2-hour peak window from the CSV we should use for the heavy synthetic runs. (action: Ellen)
   - Sign-off on the switchback window proposed (action: Tom / procurement).

Attachments and ops artifacts we will produce:
   - Stress test results document (PDF) after sizing run.
   - Canary dashboard with token-level cost + latency.
   - Rollback playbook + runbook checklists for infra and app owners.

If that looks good I will convert this into a single-page cutover timeline and route to Aditya and Marcus for capacity sizing and slot reservation.

Thanks—Mina

--
Mina Haddad
Solutions Engineering Manager, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com

Subject: Re: DealerBridge onramp - sizing validation inputs

Mina—looping in capacity and runtime owners with suggested sizing and test plan detail. Key points:

Notes / assumptions from infra:
- Model: DealerBridge will serve a 7B T5-like encoder-decoder that we've profiled at sequence=512. For strictness, we'll plan for sequence=1024 during peak synthetic runs.
- Baseline hosted token/s (avg): 1,100 tokens/s; peak concurrency in CSV ~420 concurrent requests (avg payload ~300 tokens).
- Target safety buffer: 2.0x peak concurrency for dedicated pool to cover bursty user behavior.

Sizing recommendation (initial reservation):
- GPU family: H100 80GB (preferred for KV and large context work).
- Node target: 6 x H100 (stateless worker shards), each with continuous batching tuned for 64 token-batch. This maps to an estimated sustained output of ~5,400 tokens/s with warm cache, headroom for 2.5x traffic.
- Warm-cache staging: reserve a small warm pool (2x replicas) to pre-populate KV caches during mirror runs to avoid cold-start tail latency.

Validation run specifics:
- 3-hour sizing run during your nominated peak window: ramps from 0% to 100% of sampled peak over 15 minutes, sustain for 60 minutes, then ramp down.
- Collect: P50/P95/P99 latency, token throughput, batch efficiency, GPU utilization, KV hit rate, and OCaml (sic) memory pressure stats.
- Smoke test fail triggers: P99 > 450ms for >5 consecutive minutes OR sustained GPU mem pressure > 92% for 10+ minutes.

Switchback mechanics:
- If any fail trigger occurs during canary or the 48-hour switch, we automatically route traffic back to hosted for the affected region within 15 minutes.
- Maintain a passive canary policy: keep last-known-hosted-versions pinned for 24 hours after full switchover to ease rollbacks.

Operational asks to confirm with DealerBridge:
- Do you need HIPAA-style audit logs during the shadow run? (Neha)
- Which SLOs (p99 or business KPIs) will drive acceptance? We have those mapped but need explicit alignment.

I'll prepare slot reservation once Mina confirms acceptance of 6 x H100.

—Aditya / Marcus / Kimberly

Team—confirming next steps and putting the reservation on calendar. Summary and immediate asks:

1) Slot reservation
   - Reserve: 6 x H100 (80GB) in us-west-2 for 2027-12-12 through 2027-12-18 (includes 2 days preflight and 5-day validation window).
   - Owner: Marcus (capacity ticket created: CAP-11258).

2) Validation plan (week of 12/13)

   - 12/14: 3-hour sizing run (ramp to 100% sampled peak, sustain 60m) with telemetry export to shared Drive.
   - 12/15–12/16: Canary steps (5% -> 20% -> 100% incremental steps if gates pass).

3) Acceptance criteria (restate)
   - P99 <= 450ms and <= 1.2x hosted baseline; sustained throughput >= 1.8x average token/s; error budget <0.5%

4) Switchback and rollback
   - Blackout window agreed: 00:00–04:00 PST next business day reserved for automatic switchback if triggers fire.

   - Rollback automation: Traffic control API will flip routing in <15 minutes; we keep runbook page updated with exact runbook steps.

Action items for this thread:

   - Aditya: publish test harness and schedule the 12/14 sizing run in the cluster orchestration UI.
   - Neha: confirm audit/logging hook and retention policy for the shadow runs.
   - Mina: route SOW to finance after Marcus confirms reservation.

I will stand up a single shared Slack channel (redwood-dealerbridge-onramp) and a live canary dashboard link next week. If DealerBridge can confirm the exact 2-hour peak slice by Monday we will lock the run schedule.
